_readme: Suppression list for .github/workflows/npm-advisories.yml. JSON carries no comments, so the
rules live here. The gate blocks on high/critical advisories only; moderate and low are
reported and never fail a build.
TWO LISTS, ON PURPOSE.
accepted[] — a decision. Requires `reason` (>= 10 chars, what makes this tolerable HERE) and
`expires`. On the expiry date it becomes blocking again, so an acceptance is a
dated promise to revisit, never a permanent pardon. Extending one is a commit
someone reviews.
Also requires `projects`: the projects the reason was judged for, named as the
baseline names them ('.', 'frontend', 'indexer'). The acceptance counts in those
projects and in no other. Anywhere else the advisory blocks until someone judges
it for that tree. An entry with no `projects` list counts nowhere. The same id
may have a second entry, with its own reason, for another project.
baseline   — the advisories that already existed when the gate was armed (2026-08-18),
recorded verbatim from that run. No reason is written for them because nobody
has triaged them, and inventing 32 rationales would be exactly the fabrication
this repo's honesty rule forbids. The whole baseline expires at once. After
that date every untriaged inherited advisory blocks — either fix it, or move it
into accepted[] with a real reason.
WHEN A RUN SAYS 'PRUNE'. Each project's run reports only its own suppressions whose advisory is
gone from that project. For a baseline id, delete it from that project's list. For an accepted
id, take that project out of `projects`, and delete the entry when no project is left.
THE UNIT IS THE GHSA ID, NEVER THE PACKAGE. Suppressing 'axios' would silently absorb the next
axios advisory too; suppressing GHSA-gcfj-64vw-6mp9 suppresses exactly one known finding.
KNOWN WORST ITEM IN THE BASELINE: GHSA-3gc7-fjrx-p6mg, a bigint-buffer heap overflow reachable
through @solana/spl-token in an application that signs transactions. npm reports its only fix
as a semver-major downgrade of @solana/spl-token to 0.1.8, which is a product decision and a
code change, not a lockfile bump — that is why it is baselined rather than fixed in the commit
that armed this gate, and why the baseline expiry is 90 days and not a year.

accepted.reason: Proposed on 2026-10-24, in the pull request that moves the frontend's own zod from 4.4.3 to 4.6.6, the patched release. It is carried only if the owner merges that pull request. Scope: the frontend. The flaw: before 4.6.6, zod parsed every element of an array before checking its .max(), collecting an error for each bad one, so a huge array could run the process out of memory. The 4.6.6 bump covers every copy our code imports: the browser schemas in src/ and api/_lib/proxy-schemas.js, which checks strangers' request bodies in api/supabase-proxy.js against arrays capped at .max(200). This entry carries two zod 3 copies that the advisory also covers (every version below 4.6.6) and that no zod 3 release fixes. Neither is in the site. (1) zod 3.22.4, pinned exactly by @reown/appkit-wallet 1.8.19 (1.8.24, the newest, still pins it), under @walletconnect/ethereum-provider. Its only use is the schemas for Reown's embedded-wallet frame, which ethereum-provider's @reown/appkit/core entry does not load. (2) zod 3.25.76 under @coinbase/cdp-sdk 1.56.0 (1.60.0, the newest, still asks for ^3.25.76), which @base-org/account imports only from its Node entry (payment and subscription helpers). Checked on 2026-10-24 in a vite build made with a WalletConnect project id, as production's is: AppKit is in it, but no zod 3 (its own strings ZodEffects, ZodBranded and ZodNativeEnum are absent from all 488 files) and no cdp-sdk; the only zod is 4.6.6. api/ imports neither package. If a later Reown release did bundle the frame, it would check postMessage events in the visitor's browser with no origin check, and the worst a hostile window could do is run that one tab out of memory. Forcing zod 4 under either package is a major-version override under code we do not own, the move NOTES.md 2026-10-06 shows can break quietly. npm's suggested fix, @base-org/account 2.5.5, still depends on cdp-sdk and keeps appkit-wallet's copy, so it fixes nothing. Expires with the baseline. It can go when both packages move to zod 4.6.6 or later, or drop zod.

Proposed on 2026-10-21, in the same pull request that clears this advisory from the frontend with vite 8.3.3. It is carried only if the owner merges that pull request. Scope: the indexer. The flaw (published 2026-10-20) is in launch-editor, which vite bundles and serves at /__open-in-editor on its dev server: on Windows a crafted file path passes the existence check and reaches a shell command. The fix on this line is vite 6.4.4 and there is no safe way to reach it. ponder 0.8.33 pins vite at exactly 5.0.7, beside vite-node 1.0.2, which asks for vite ^5, so the fix is a major-version override under the loader ponder runs every indexing file through. ponder 0.18.2, the newest, does not clear it either: it pins vite 8.3.1, which is affected. No request reaches the flaw here. ponder calls vite's createServer only to load ponder.config.ts and the indexing files through vite-node. It never calls listen() on that server, and its own HTTP server (hono) mounts none of vite's middlewares, so /__open-in-editor is on no port (read in ponder 0.8.33's dist/bin/ponder.js on 2026-10-21). The flaw also needs Windows, and production runs on Railway's Linux containers. Expires with the baseline so the indexer's ponder 0.8 debt comes due together. It can go when the indexer moves to a ponder whose vite is 6.4.4, 7.3.7, 8.1.6, 8.2.4 or 8.3.3 or later on its line.
